note: A three-arrow protection / bromination / deprotection scheme, compressed into the single reaction record the schema allows. As drawn, left to right: aniline --(CH3CO)2O over the arrow, Pyridine under it--> N-phenylethanamide (acetanilide), drawn as a benzene ring bearing H-N-C(=O)-CH3; --Br2 over the arrow, CH3COOH under it--> the para-brominated amide, captioned '(Major)', drawn as the same H-N-C(=O)-CH3 ring with Br at the position opposite the nitrogen; --'OH- or H+' over the arrow--> 4-bromoaniline. The recorded reaction keeps only the overall transformation (aniline to 4-bromoaniline) and places every reagent written over or under the three arrows into the agents field in the order drawn: acetic anhydride, pyridine, Br2, acetic acid, hydroxide and proton. The two intermediates are therefore NOT in the reaction SMILES; for a reader who needs them they are CC(=O)NC1=CC=CC=C1 (acetanilide) and CC(=O)NC1=CC=C(Br)C=C1 (4-bromoacetanilide, the major product). The last structure carries printed ring-position numbers 1, 2 and 3 on the ipso, ortho and meta carbons; these are annotation, not atoms. All rings are drawn Kekule (alternating inner lines, no circle). No stereochemistry is drawn. Confidence is probable because of the loss of the two intermediates in the compression, not because any drawn atom was unclear.
